blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: problem recognition — Determine what problem is being solved and its computational form.
divide and conquer — Divide input, solve smaller instances, combine results.
constraint — Condition a valid solution must satisfy.
tractability — Whether an algorithm can solve realistic sizes with feasible resources.

blocks.title: Recognise ambiguity
blocks.text: 'Fair' is subjective until objective criteria are supplied, such as balancing first-period lessons across teachers.

blocks.title: Make requirements testable
blocks.text: Represent rooms, lessons and slots; specify hard constraints and a success test.

blocks.title: Select techniques appropriately
blocks.text: Decompose into assign/check/evaluate modules. Divide and conquer is useful where subproblems can be solved and combined consistently; not every decomposition is divide and conquer.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict the method
blocks.text: Replace vague 'best' with a measurable objective such as minimum total travel time.

blocks.title: Worked example · Check and explain
blocks.text: Specify route constraints and verify a produced route covers all required locations.
